en: To continue doing something; or to continue to behave in a particular way.
ex: Please carry on with your work.
請繼續你的工作。

en: To form the parts of something; or to invent a story; or to put on cosmetics; or to become friends again after a quarrel.
ex: Women make up half of the team.
女性占了團隊的一半。

en: To drive a vehicle to the side of the road and stop.
ex: The officer told him to pull over.
警官要他把車開到路邊停下。

en: To reach a particular total; or to wake up after being unconscious; or to refer to a subject.
ex: When it comes to math, she is a genius.
說到數學，她是個天才。

en: To produce a sound, light, smell or other effect.
ex: The flowers gave forth a sweet smell.
花朵散發出甜美的香氣。

en: To become quiet and relaxed after being angry, excited or nervous.
ex: Calm down and tell me what happened.
冷靜下來告訴我發生了什麼事。

en: To telephone someone who called you earlier; or to ask for something to be returned.
ex: I'll call you back in five minutes.
我五分鐘後回你電話。

en: To end a telephone call; or to put something on a hook or hanger.
ex: She hung up before I could say goodbye.
她在我來得及說再見之前就掛了電話。

en: To go with someone to the place they are leaving from and say goodbye.
ex: We went to the station to see him off.
我們到車站為他送行。

en: To have a good relationship with someone; or to manage or make progress.
ex: The two sisters get along very well.
這對姊妹相處得很好。

en: To suggest an idea or plan; or to use energy or effort; or to produce leaves or buds.
ex: She put forth a new theory about dinosaurs.
她提出了一個關於恐龍的新理論。

en: To put on clothes to see if they fit; or to test something to see if you like it.
ex: Can I try on this jacket?
我可以試穿這件夾克嗎？

en: To be connected with or concern something.
col: what it has to do with
ex: This has nothing to do with you.
這跟你沒有關係。

en: To make someone look silly or stupid.
ex: Don't make a fool of yourself in public.
別在公共場合出洋相。

en: To suddenly start doing something such as laughing or crying; or to suddenly enter a place.
ex: The audience burst into applause.
觀眾突然爆出掌聲。

en: To be wasted or to have no result.
col: go for nothing in the end
all his efforts went for nothing
ex: All our hard work went for nothing.
我們所有的努力都白費了。

en: To give or pass something to the next person.
ex: Please hand on this letter to the director.
請把這封信轉交給主任。

en: To continue for a very long and boring time; or to pull something along the ground.
ex: The meeting dragged on until midnight.
會議一直拖到半夜。

en: To go in front of people who are waiting in a line without waiting for your turn.
col: cut in line at the bank
ex: It's rude to cut in line.
插隊是很沒禮貌的。

en: To think that you are better than someone else; or to look at something from a higher place.
ex: You shouldn't look down on anyone.
你不應該瞧不起任何人。

en: To spend time doing nothing useful.
ex: Don't just sit around; help me clean.
別光坐著，來幫我打掃。

en: To escape from someone who is holding you; or to leave a group or a country and start something separate.
ex: The prisoner broke away from the guards.
囚犯掙脫了警衛。

en: To take care of someone or something.
ex: Who is looking after the kids today?
今天誰在照顧孩子們？

en: To have the same opinion as someone.
ex: We don't always see eye to eye.
我們的看法並不總是一致。

en: To do something that is more than is acceptable or reasonable.
col: this time you went too far
ex: You went too far when you insulted her.
你侮辱她就太過分了。

en: To become so excited or frightened that you can't think clearly.
ph: lose one's head in a crisis
ex: Don't lose your head in an emergency.
緊急情況下不要慌亂。

en: To begin a journey; or to make something explode; or to cause something to start.
ex: We set off at six in the morning.
我們早上六點出發。

en: To visit a place for a short time; or (of a train or ship) to stop at a place.
ex: The train calls at every station.
這班火車每站都停。

en: To use something or someone for a purpose.
ex: Make good use of your time.
好好利用你的時間。

en: To get rid of something that you do not want; or to deal with something.
ex: Please dispose of the rubbish properly.
請妥善處理垃圾。

en: To quarrel with someone and stop being friendly.
ex: They fell out with each other over money.
他們為了錢鬧翻了。

en: To decide something after thinking about it.
ex: I can't make up my mind what to wear.
我拿不定主意要穿什麼。

en: To continue to communicate with someone.
ex: We promised to stay in touch.
我們約定保持聯絡。

en: To do something again; or to decorate a room again.
ex: I have to do this essay over.
我得把這篇文章重寫。

en: To continue to follow a plan, belief or rule and not change it.
ex: She held to her belief despite the criticism.
儘管受到批評，她仍堅守自己的信念。

en: To go with someone to the place they leave from and say goodbye.
ph: see someone off at the airport
ex: We saw them off at the airport.
我們在機場為他們送行。

en: To be successful in life or in a career; or to last a long time.
ex: With her talent, she will go far.
以她的才華，她會大有前途。

en: To suddenly meet a problem or difficulty.
ex: We ran up against a lot of problems.
我們遇到了許多問題。

en: To sit with your back straight; or to stay awake at night instead of going to bed.
ex: He sat up all night studying for the exam.
他為了準備考試熬了一整夜。

en: To ask someone to come and help; or to telephone a place.
ex: We had to call in a plumber to fix the leak.
我們得請水管工來修漏水。
